text:
What if the future isn't about choosing between AI and humanity? Maybe it's about making sure we don't lose the second while building the first.

Being a mom to a three-year-old has completely changed the way I learn. Alright, alright, the way I live.

These days, most of my studying happens late at night. While watching recordings of our design AI workshops, I caught myself slowing down. Watching people laugh at themselves, struggle to explain an idea, ask the same question twenty times until it finally clicks. Real humans figuring things out together. I actually paused the recording. I needed to stay with that feeling for a moment. It felt alive.

I'm not escaping technology. I'm learning it. But it feels like the faster the world moves, the more intentionally we need to protect the things that remind us we're alive.

Twenty years ago, I would have laughed if someone had told me that one day I'd dream about a small house, a garden, and peace. Young me wanted to be Miranda Priestly. Forty-year-old me thinks my grandma's farm lifestyle is the dream.

Or this is just what turning 40 looks like — you realize you're choosing the main character for the next decade, and somehow yours turns out to be a farmer. 🌱 Okay, a farmer with AI helpers.
